newsitem.title: USA: CBOT new crop corn hits two-month high on weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT new crop corn hits two-month high on weather.

text.p: CBOT new crop corn futures opened higher on Wednesday and the December contract hit a two-month high on outlooks for continued dry weather in the central U.S. Midwest, pit sources said.

Forecasts called for dry weather through Friday with temperatures expected to warm up this weekend. Long-range forecasts suggested no significant rainfall for Illinois through August 6, meteorologists said.
Dry weather in the North China Plain corn growing region also garnered attention. Trade sources said recent rains came too late to reverse the effects of moisture stress.
At 0950 CDT, corn was up 6-1/4 to two cents per bushel with December up 5-3/4 at $2.66.
The December contract peaked at $2.66-1/2, the highest since May 16.
In opening trade, Cargill Inc bought one million bushels December and bull spread five million December/July at 15-1/2 cents, premium July, trader said.
